end.parentNote: Asha practised the pattern using square arrangements and counting the added L-shaped layer. Saanvi correctly identified 1 + 3 + 5 + 7 = 16 and later found 25 for the 5-by-5 square. They first counted the shared corner twice, then corrected this by using 5 + 5 - 1 = 9; the general pattern for longer odd-number sums still needs practice. At home, draw square dot patterns for 1, 4, 9, and 16 and label the odd-number layer added each time.
